messages:
kevin: Heads-up — us-central racks r12-r14 have a persistent egress/NIC queue saturation starting ~06:10 UTC. Seen for ~40m, correlates to pod label tenant=analytics-prod. p99 tail latency for small-gen doubled.
ops-bot: ALERT: net.egress_queue_depth > 90% on hosts r12-14 (since 06:12). Triggered by flow fingerprint 0x7a3b.
kevin: Here's a quick log sample from one host (r12-03):
```
[06:15:03] NIC tx_queue=94% drop=0.8% pkts_requeued=1200
[06:15:04] process=llm_infer tenant=analytics-prod pid=14211 cpu=78%
```
lina: Yikes. Is it definitely noisy neighbor (single tenant) vs upstream egress flapping? any cross-tenant correlation?
sree: I ran a quick query — the spike maps to 3 pods across 2 nodes, same image + heavy streaming requests. No other tenants show the same pattern. likely noisy.
kevin: Agree. Candidate mitigations: 1) move those pods to dedicated-burst pool (soft carve) 2) apply per-tenant egress policer (rate-limit) 3) bump nic qdisc to prioritize control plane. All have tradeoffs.
elaine: Cost note: carving a dedicated fractional slice in us-central for that tenant adds ~2.1k/mo (est) for reserved capacity during the busy window. If we do temporary dedicated carve, ops needs an approval ticket.
sree: Could we instead route analytics-prod traffic to eu-west spare capacity during their heavy windows? replication concerns but might be cheaper than dedicated on-demand.
kevin: Cross-region routing OK for non-PHI workloads; analytics-prod is borderline but ok per app-owner. Downsides: increased latency (~40ms), egress billing different.
elaine: @kevin please add a cost calc: monthly delta, and a 7-day sim of carveout vs policer. ops will weigh.
kevin: Will do. Quick experiment plan I can run now:
```bash
# mark pods for soft-move to fractional-dedicated pool
kubectl label pod -l app=analytics,env=prod infra.carve=intent-dedicated-temp --overwrite
# then run routing weight bump for dedicated pool for 1h
redwoodctl routing adjust --region usw1 --from shared --to fractional-dedicated --weight 0.6 --duration 1h
```
ops-bot: SCHEDULED: routing weight change requested by kevin, ETA 06:45 UTC. Will auto-rollback at end of duration unless confirmed.
elaine: If you do that, tag the ticket with cost_estimate and set paging off for the window (low risk ops). :thumbsup:
sree: If routing works, follow-up: implement soft egress policer on the tenant as permanent guard (rate=120Mbps burst=15MB) and reduce need for carveouts.
kevin: Plan: run canary on r12-03 and r13-01 first, monitor registry: net.egress_queue_depth, p99 gen latency, and billing meters. Will post results in 30m.
deploy-bot: deploy will proceed to canary nodes r12-03,r13-01 at 06:46 (10 pods).
kevin: Thanks — will update thread with numbers. If carveout reduces tail by >30% and cost delta < est, ops will approve a 24h temporary carve then transition to policer.
